title: A directed colimit of algebraic spaces glued by thickenings is a formal algebraic space
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter formal-spaces.tex (Formal Algebraic Spaces)
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file formal-spaces.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a directed system of algebraic spaces whose transition maps are thickenings, the colimit taken in fppf sheaves is a formal algebraic space (statement lines 2972-2979). The proof builds the required covering explicitly. The colimit is a sheaf by construction; a member of the system is fixed and an etale covering of it by affine schemes is chosen, which exists by a general statement on coverings of algebraic spaces by affines (proof lines 2981-2987). The covering is then propagated along the system: for each later member there is a cartesian diagram with etale vertical arrows whose existence is the topological invariance of the etale site under thickenings, and these diagrams are unique up to unique isomorphism, so the pieces are compatible along the system, the transition maps between them are thickenings as base changes of thickenings, and each piece is an affine scheme because the fibre product of an affine scheme over a thickening is again affine (proof lines 2987-3003). Taking the colimit of the pieces yields an affine formal algebraic space, and the resulting morphism to the colimit of the members is etale because any morphism from an affine scheme into the colimit factors through a member -- a step the author marks as omitted (proof lines 3003-3011). The claim is H2: two constructions are used in earnest, the propagation of an etale covering along a system of thickenings with its uniqueness, and the reduction of the affineness of the pieces to a statement on limits of spaces, with only the factorisation step left unproved.
